title: The Span of Coverage Months a Ridgecrest RxSecure Settlement Figure Runs Over
content:
The span of coverage months a settlement figure runs over on a Ridgecrest RxSecure stand-alone Medicare Part D prescription drug plan account is read from the standing of the enrollment and the cadence on which the plan bills the premium.

| Standing of the enrollment | Cadence on which the plan bills the premium | The coverage months the figure runs over |
| --- | --- | --- |
| In its premium grace period | monthly | every coverage month the account has charged for since coverage began |
| In its premium grace period | quarterly | the coverage months the account has charged for in the 6 months up to the handling date |
| In force | monthly | the coverage months the account has charged for in the 3 months up to the handling date |
| In force | quarterly | the coverage months the account has charged for in the 3 months up to the handling date |
| Terminated, or standing on any other footing | either cadence | the coverage months the account has charged for in the 3 months up to the handling date |

Both parts of each of the first two rows must hold together: the enrollment must stand in its premium grace period **and** the cadence must be the one named. An enrollment in force falls to the 3-month span whichever cadence it is billed on.

## Worked on a hypothetical account

Take an account that has charged premium for 11 coverage months since coverage began, of which 6 fall in the 6 months up to the handling date and 3 in the 3 months up to the handling date.

- In its premium grace period and billed monthly: the figure runs over all 11 coverage months.
- In its premium grace period and billed quarterly: the figure runs over the 6 coverage months in the 6-month window.
- In force, on either cadence: the figure runs over the 3 coverage months in the 3-month window.

Each window is counted back from the handling date, and each gathers the coverage months the account has actually charged for, not calendar months in which nothing was charged.
